prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-24, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-24):
| Current ratio           | 0.63 |
| Retained earnings       | -5,086M |
| Current liabilities     | 3,973M |
| Current assets          | 2,495M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 3,652M |
| Total liabilities       | 52,835M |
| Total assets            | 63,190M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,161M |
| Revenue                 | 2,738M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows severe liquidity stress (current ratio ≈ 0.63) and very high leverage with positive but small equity (negative retained earnings, equity ~5.8% of assets) alongside a very high debt burden relative to EBIT, indicating substantial default risk and fragile solvency.

DECISION: CCC+
